author: Codex difficulty36_a04

source_artifacts.claim: The ferry helper sets an eight-second period; current level_10 authors the 210-pixel vertical lift, attached STOP, landing/bridge, roles and exits.
Level_01 introduced a powered lift needing a two-person RESTORE latch.
Level_03 introduced Isp STOP on a moving ferry and Pac RESCUE progression latch.
Level_04 introduced Pac STEADY to stabilize a bridge and Isp RESCUE latch.
Level_07 practiced role-specific STEADY and RESCUE around a bridge and ferry.
Moving, unstable and attached-pad types; pad effects and barrier ownership.
An attached pad follows its platform; hold/latch occupancy and door/motor/stabilize effects.
Unstabilized bridges collapse after their authored occupancy interval and can respawn.
Hazard contact causes death; both matching exits are required, collectibles are separate.
Movement, jump, and rider handling for the source-inferred broad landings.
Closed barriers block only their designated hero.
Two distinct hero control sets and R restart mapping; no keyboard hardware was tested.

prior_knowledge.concept: A two-person latch can power a lift. Level_10 reuses the lift idea but the elevator moves continuously and an attached STOP freezes it near the upper landing instead of requiring RESTORE power.

evidence.claim: Level_01 uses a two-weight RESTORE latch to power a required-power lift.
Level_10 starts both heroes aboard a continuously moving lift with an Isp-only attached STOP.

prior_knowledge.concept: Isp STOP can brake moving machinery; level_03 introduced it for a ferry, and level_07 practiced a related ferry stop. Here STOP is attached to the elevator and also opens Pac’s landing gate.

evidence.claim: Level_03 authors a moving ferry and Isp STOP motor control.
Level_07 practiced STOP on a ferry while Pac operates STEADY.
Level_10 attaches STOP to the lift and opens Pac’s landing barrier.

prior_knowledge.concept: Pac STEADY holds an unstable bridge and Isp RESCUE can latch route access; level_04 introduced those paired roles. Level_10 repeats them above a slime gap and extends RESCUE to stabilize the bridge and open all gates.

evidence.claim: Level_04 has Pac STEADY stabilize a bridge and Isp RESCUE latch progression.
Current STEADY opens Isp bridge access; RESCUE stabilizes the bridge and opens progression doors.

prior_knowledge.concept: The previous two rooms provided heavy cargo/team-push and split-lane route cues, but neither is required for this elevator route; their screen exposure does not imply mastery.

evidence.claim: The immediately preceding locked first-pass record identifies the level_09 exposure and its limits.
Current room has no crate or split-lane cargo requirement.

mechanics.fact: Both heroes start aboard a continuously powered 270-pixel-wide elevator. It travels vertically 210 pixels on an 8-second cycle, reaching the top around the four-second point. Isp’s STOP pad is attached to the lift; occupying it turns off the motor and opens Pac’s landing gate. Isp must stop near the top for the landing to be within jump reach.

evidence.claim: The ferry helper sets an eight-second cycle; both spawns are on the 270-pixel lift with 210-pixel vertical travel and attached Isp STOP.
Attached pad coordinates follow the platform; STOP turns off motor, and powered moving platforms follow their motion period.
Shared jump arc supports reaching the landing when the lift is near its upper end.

mechanics.fact: Pac-only STEADY is a hold pad on the landing; while Pac occupies it, it stabilizes the unstable bridge and opens Isp’s bridge barrier. The bridge otherwise collapses after 0.8 seconds of occupancy and respawns after 2 seconds.

evidence.claim: Defines bridge, STEADY effects, and Isp-specific barrier.
Unstable-platform and stabilization effect types.
Hold-pad stabilization and natural bridge collapse/respawn behavior.

mechanics.fact: Isp-only RESCUE is a persistent latch that opens Pac landing, Isp bridge and Pac finish gates and continues stabilizing the bridge. Once latched, Pac can leave STEADY and cross.

evidence.claim: Lists the RESCUE latch and all door/stabilize effects.
Latch remains active after its owner leaves and effects hold the route open.

mechanics.fact: The two slime pools lie below the lift approach and bridge. A fall into either pool is lethal; both heroes still must overlap their own exits. The blue and orange sparks are owner-specific but do not gate completion.

evidence.claim: Defines slime pools, owner-specific collectibles and distinct exits.
Hazard contact kills; completion requires both matching exits and collectibles are separate.

legal_routes.name: Current-source elevator, role-handoff, and bridge route (inferred; old browser route corroborates only its archived build)

steps.goal: Ride the shared elevator toward the upper landing.
steps.action: Remain aboard the broad lift as it rises. Let it approach the upper end of its travel; the four-second idle image shows it near the landing but contains no player action.
steps.expected_feedback: The lift is moving upward and repeats its vertical route; it can be stopped at a useful height.

evidence.claim: Both spawns are on the lift; its motion and attached STOP are authored.
At the idle four-second capture the lift has risen close to the landing; no input is shown.

steps.goal: Hold the elevator near the upper landing and open Pac’s route.
steps.action: Move Isp onto the attached STOP when the lift is high enough for the landing jump, then remain there while Pac moves across.
steps.expected_feedback: The lift motor stops and Pac’s full-height landing barrier opens.

evidence.claim: Isp STOP is attached to the lift and opens Pac landing.
Attached pad tracks lift; active STOP disables its motor and opens the door.

steps.goal: Reach and hold STEADY on the upper landing.
steps.action: Jump from the stopped lift to the nearby landing and stand on Pac STEADY while Isp remains on STOP.
steps.expected_feedback: STEADY stabilizes the bridge and opens the Isp-only bridge barrier.

evidence.claim: Landing, bridge, Pac STEADY and Isp gate positions/effects.
The hold pad stabilizes the bridge while occupied.

steps.goal: Cross the bridge and latch the final route.
steps.action: Leave STOP after Pac is holding STEADY, jump from lift to landing, pass Pac onto the bridge, cross to Isp RESCUE and activate it.
steps.expected_feedback: RESCUE latches, keeps bridge stable, and opens the remaining route barriers.

evidence.claim: Bridge access, Isp RESCUE position, and latch effects.
The latch persists after release and stabilizes the bridge.

steps.action: After RESCUE, Pac leaves STEADY and crosses the now-stable bridge; each hero moves to its own exit on the finish platform.
steps.expected_feedback: The latch keeps progression doors open and completion occurs when both matching exits are occupied.

evidence.claim: RESCUE opens Pac’s finish gate; final floor and exits.
Both matching exits are necessary for completion.
Current source lays out a continuous route through the elevator, landing, role pads, bridge and exits.
An archived route note describes the same role order.
The old-build trace reaches complete with both heroes at exits; it does not prove current runtime.
Frozen first-pass cooperation estimate being compared.
Current room objective, role instructions, dialogue and idle-only method.
Current canvas layout around the lift, upper bridge and exits.
The index classifies this room as historical-trace, not current-replayed.
Bounded current-native probe found no reusable trace; that is not evidence of impossibility or failure.

isp: Ride the shared elevator and occupy attached STOP near the upper landing; this brakes the lift and opens Pac’s landing gate.
After Pac holds STEADY, leave STOP, cross the bridge, and latch RESCUE to hold the route open for Pac.
pac: Ride the shared elevator, jump to the upper landing after Isp opens it, and hold STEADY to stabilize the bridge and open Isp’s route.
After Isp latches RESCUE, cross the stabilized bridge and reach Pac’s matching exit.

common_mistakes.mistake: Isp activates attached STOP while the lift is still low.
common_mistakes.consequence: The lift freezes and Pac’s barrier opens, but the landing remains too high for the intended jump.
common_mistakes.recovery: Step off STOP so the lift resumes its cycle, remain aboard, and stop again nearer the upper landing. This is a source-derived reversible correction, not a separately replayed recovery.

evidence.claim: Lift travel distance, attached STOP, and upper landing height.
Movement and jump behavior allow leaving/re-entering the pad; precise recovery was not replayed.
Historical route stops only after riding near the upper landing.

common_mistakes.mistake: Pac leaves STEADY before Isp reaches RESCUE.
common_mistakes.consequence: The bridge loses stabilization and can collapse after 0.8 seconds while Isp is crossing; a fall can land in lethal slime.
common_mistakes.recovery: If Isp survives, the bridge respawns after 2 seconds and Pac can re-enter STEADY before the next crossing attempt. If either hero dies, restart with R and repeat the lift/bridge sequence. The re-hold path is source-supported but was not replayed for this room.

evidence.claim: Bridge collapse threshold, Pac hold pad, rescue latch, and slime below.
Unstabilized bridge collapses/respawns; slime contact is lethal.
R restarts the level.

common_mistakes.mistake: A hero misses the jump from the lift/landing or falls from the bridge.
common_mistakes.consequence: A missed landing may drop the player into one of the slime pools; source marks slime contact as lethal.
common_mistakes.recovery: Use R to restart and repeat the shared ride and role handoff. This repeats a moderate route segment; no current room-specific recovery trace is available.

evidence.claim: Vertical lift, elevated landing/bridge, and hazards beneath them.
Slime contact or falling beyond the world height ends the run.
R restarts the current room.
No reusable level_10 route/recovery trace was present in the bounded replay selection.

optional_collectibles: Isp-only lift_blue spark at x340,y275 along the elevator’s rising path.
Pac-only landing_orange spark at x665,y275 above the landing. Neither is required for both-exit completion.

reasoning.rationale: The visible instruction “ride up, brake upstairs” points directly to Isp’s STOP pad, and the visible Pac STEADY/bridge labels suggest the next role. Source confirms a short ordered chain—stop the lift high, let Pac hold the bridge, then Isp latches RESCUE. There are several handoffs, but the intended plan is cued rather than obscure.

evidence.claim: Dialogue explicitly says ride up and brake upstairs; the UI names roles and exits.
STOP, STEADY, split bridge and exit labels appear in sequence on the canvas.
Source gives the ordered STOP/STEADY/RESCUE effects.

cooperation.rationale: Both roles have indispensable work in sequence: Isp brakes and opens the landing, Pac holds STEADY to let Isp cross, then Isp latches RESCUE to release Pac. This is more than one handoff, but once RESCUE is latched no simultaneous movement is required.

evidence.claim: Isp and Pac pads have distinct owners and crossing effects.
The paired bridge roles were previously introduced, but current source confirms they are mandatory here.
Historical route uses the same handoff sequence.

execution.rationale: Both players ride the wide 270-pixel lift; Isp and Pac make controlled jumps to the 150-pixel landing and 180-pixel bridge. The heights and lethal gaps matter, but the surfaces are broad and the bridge can be held stable, so the route does not demand sustained precision.

evidence.claim: Lift, landing, bridge widths and heights.
Shared jump arc is large enough for the authored 42-pixel lift-to-landing height when the lift is stopped near the top.
Historical path uses broad surfaces and controlled jumps; it is not a current play measurement.

timing.rationale: Isp must stop the cycling lift near its upper landing; stopping too low is reversible by releasing STOP and waiting for the next rise. The lift repeats every eight seconds and has a broad approach window, and Pac can hold STEADY until RESCUE latches, so there is no chained narrow window.

evidence.claim: The lift helper period and current authored vertical motion support a repeatable eight-second ride that STOP can freeze.
Powered moving platforms follow repeatable motion and stop when their motor is off.
The historical route waits for the upper part of the ride rather than requiring a precision instant.

hazards.rationale: The mandatory lift-to-landing and bridge route crosses above two authored slime pools. Both gaps have wide platform support when the lift is stopped and the bridge is held, but a missed jump can fall into lethal slime.

evidence.claim: The lift shaft and bridge are visibly above open green hazard regions.
Hazards lie beneath both required transitions.
Slime contact is lethal.

novelty.rationale: Level_01 already introduced a lift; level_03 Isp STOP on a ferry; and level_04 Pac STEADY plus Isp RESCUE on an unstable bridge. This room recombines those familiar roles into a vertical lift-to-bridge handoff, rather than teaching several new mechanics.

evidence.claim: Earlier lift power and STOP-on-ferry mechanics.
Earlier Pac STEADY / Isp RESCUE bridge roles.
Current composition attaches STOP to the elevator and chains it to the bridge handoff.

recovery_cost.rationale: Stopping too low can be corrected by stepping off and waiting for another lift pass. A premature STEADY release can collapse the bridge, with a two-second respawn if Isp survives; falling into slime instead forces a restart and repetition of the ride and handoff. These are more than immediate retries, but not a long cargo setup.

evidence.claim: Source geometry and authored bridge/slime consequences.
Bridge respawn and lethal hazard behavior.
R restart mapping.
No current room-specific miss/recovery trace was indexed.

solution_clarity.rationale: The dialogue says “ride up, brake upstairs”; the canvas labels Isp STOP, Pac STEADY and RESCUE beside the corresponding structures, and the idle screenshots show the lift rise toward the landing. “My glucose isn’t free” is a misleading joke rather than a required gate: source contains no glucose condition in this room.

evidence.claim: Visible dialogue supplies ride/brake cues and the both-exit objective.
Canvas shows the color/role labels on the intended route.
Idle screenshot shows the lift near the upper landing without any player action.
Room source has no glucose gate or glucose resource requirement.

control_friction.rationale: The source maps distinct movement and jump keys, but no shared-keyboard hardware trial verified rollover, reach, or simultaneous-input reliability.

evidence.claim: Lists separate hero controls; the packet contains no player keypress.
Browser runtime maps separate key sets but cannot establish physical-keyboard reliability.

confidence_reason: Current source and shared engine mechanics establish the lift period, attached STOP, landing gate, unstable bridge, slime consequence, and role handoffs. A historical browser completion corroborates the route on an older build; there is no retained current-room input trace or miss/retry probe. Current runtime equivalence, novice discovery, mistake frequency, and human demand remain unobserved.

confirmed: The visible “ride up, brake upstairs” text and ISP STOP/PAC STEADY cues correctly pointed to a role-sequenced lift/bridge route.
The visible split bridge is part of the mandatory route, and both heroes have different roles before their matching exits.
missed_mechanics: Both heroes start aboard a continuous 270-pixel lift; it rises and returns on an eight-second period, and Isp’s attached STOP freezes it near the upper landing while opening Pac’s gate.
Pac’s hold STEADY stabilizes the unstable bridge and opens the Isp-only crossing; Isp RESCUE latches, keeps the bridge stable and opens the remaining gates.
The two slime pools are authored beneath mandatory transitions, making a missed lift/bridge landing lethal; the two sparks are optional and owner-specific.
The “glucose” dialogue does not correspond to a gate or payment mechanic in this room.
incorrect_inferences: No firm first-pass route claim was contradicted. The proposed concern about a glucose gate was explicitly left as unknown; source resolves it as a misleading joke, not an actual condition.
changed_judgments: Reasoning remains 2 because the source confirms a clear ordered dependency that the visible ride/brake and color-role labels already suggested; no hidden multi-branch plan is required.
Cooperation changed from 2 to 3 because source confirms Isp STOP, Pac STEADY, then Isp RESCUE are all required; Pac’s bridge hold enables Isp, and Isp’s latch then frees Pac.
Execution remains 2 because both characters cross broad lift/landing/bridge surfaces with a few controlled jumps, rather than sustained precision movement.

Timing changed from null to 1 because the lift must be stopped near the upper landing, but its eight-second cycle repeats and stopping too low can be undone by waiting for another rise; Pac can safely hold STEADY until RESCUE.
Hazards changed from null to 2 because the mandatory route passes above lethal slime pools, although the wide lift and held bridge provide safe support.
Novelty remains 2: lift, STOP, STEADY and RESCUE were introduced earlier; the room recombines them into a vertical-to-bridge handoff.

Recovery changed from null to 2 because an early stop can be reversed, while a bridge-collapse miss can require respawn/re-hold or a death restart that repeats the ride and handoff. This recovery is source-inferred, not replayed.

Solution clarity remains 1 because screenshots and dialogue expose the main roles and sequence; the glucose line is nonliteral and no actual glucose condition is authored. Control friction remains null without a hardware trial.
unresolved: Whether the current browser build follows the source-derived route; the only retained completion is from an older served bundle and the bounded native probe had no reusable trace.
Whether a new pair recognizes that STOP is attached to the moving lift and should be activated near its upper end from the idle screenshots.
Whether a premature bridge release is noticed and recovered before either player falls; no current miss/retry probe exists.
Human completion time, error rate, frustration, control rollover, and single-operator interference are unmeasured.

single_operator_note: One operator must ride and brake with Isp while steering Pac from the lift to STEADY, then return attention to Isp for the bridge/RESCUE step, and finally move Pac after the latch. The source-derived route does not require simultaneous movement, but the character switching and held-pad coordination add one-person control demands; these were not tested.
